label: 71-improve-c
method: Every one of 71-review-b's 14 findings applied or declined. Stale sibling pointers were rewritten by name to the skill that survived the fold (build-adapter-pair, build-definition-of-done, build-evidence-record and build-interface-versioning all resolve to build-evidence; cap-consumption to agentic-stack; xc-enforcement-chain to xc-guarantees), in the body, inside every folded object and in references/usage.md, with the sentences that named two removed skills at once rewritten by hand rather than substituted. Folded composes_with lists were remapped through docs/fold/plan.json and deduplicated. Two definitions of done were re-measured with tools/measure.py and their expected texts regenerated with tools/expected_from_measured.py. After every edit: python3 tools/render_skill.py .claude/skills/<skill> && python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill>.

applied.change: The folded implement facet no longer ships a second second-adapter. folded['cap-isolation-implement'].adapters[1] is now E-swap-candidate-gvisor, the row RP-005 recorded, with maps_to, cannot and swap_procedure written for userspace syscall interception (no guest kernel, no block-device root, no hardware-level isolation claim) and the swap_procedure naming RP-005 as what replaced the earlier component-sandbox candidate; the facet's entities list was updated with it. The definition of done no longer leaves the second adapter unnamed: expected_design now says that `--adapter second` is the binding standing for E-swap-candidate-gvisor - a unit granted a capability set with no kernel and no filesystem, instantiated without a boot.
Removed with R71B-001: the row the X-cap-isolation-004 gVisor quote anchors now describes gVisor, so the cited record supports the claim. The quote and its sources are unchanged.

expected_failure_design rewritten from a reproduced run of breakage A (applied and reverted by hand before the rewrite, then again by tools/measure.py): both adapters report egress_attempts_blocked=0 against egress_attempts_made=3 and fail the conformance check `every egress attempt was blocked`, which fails the five gate checks that need a clean conformance run (dryrun conformance exits 0; no check failed; before the swap, conformance passes; after the swap, conformance passes; both technologies in one run) and section 5's `a runtime that claimed cancellation and missed it is told apart from one that never claimed it`, whose 'never claimed' adapter row now carries the failed egress assertion; jail-mode, marker, identity, digest and cross-adapter assertions still pass, section 4 still passes, and the gate ends `passed 19, failed 6`, so the conformance command after the && never runs. The old claim that the report is green on everything except the egress property is gone. Re-measured: tools/measure.py cap-isolation with the breakage-A and git-checkout restore commands -> measured at 4445dfd, clean exit 0, breakage exit 1, restore verified; tools/expected_from_measured.py cap-isolation regenerated expected and expected_failure. The fix also asked for harness/containment/README.md row 4 to be corrected in the same pass; that file is outside this step's scope, so the design text records that the README still carries the old claim.

Every prose pointer now names a skill that exists and the part it owns: instructions[5] and best_practices[0] and [4] point at build-evidence for the adapter-pair rule; instructions[7] reads 'agentic-stack and build-evidence carry the rule that a criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion (F-part-c-04) ... and build-evidence's adapter-pair rule requires the one suite to run over both adapters'; the folded facet's instructions[8] pair (which named build-definition-of-done and build-evidence-record in one sentence) was rewritten to one pointer at build-evidence; folded composes_with.builds_on is now ['build-evidence','cap-isolation']; references/usage.md now says the caller doctrine is stated once in agentic-stack, which absorbed the former cap-consumption in the row-71 fold.
Description trigger clause narrowed from 'where the real credential lives' to 'why no real secret enters the unit', leaving issuance and delegation to cap-identity.

The definition of done is no longer cap-isolation's criterion character for character. The criterion now runs the gate and the conformance run, keeps each exit status, and ends with a command that re-reads the conformance report and prints, per adapter, stop_reason and declared_gap_honoured, exiting non-zero unless the gate passed, the conformance run passed, both adapters honoured their declared gap and the two stop reasons are exactly cancelled and cancel_timeout. Because that command runs on both the clean and the broken path, the rendered table now shows this skill's property in both directions: Expected 'adapter=simulated-machine-unit stop_reason=cancelled declared_gap_honoured=true | adapter=capability-granted-unit stop_reason=cancel_timeout declared_gap_honoured=true'; Expected failure 'adapter=simulated-machine-unit stop_reason=cancel_timeout declared_gap_honoured=false | adapter=capability-granted-unit stop_reason=cancel_timeout declared_gap_honoured=true'. expected_design records what the last command asserts and expected_failure_design adds that the gate fails five checks with breakage B. Re-measured: tools/measure.py cap-agent-runtime with breakage B (cancel_poll_interval_s=30) and the git-checkout restore -> measured at 3ad234e, clean exit 0, breakage exit 1, restore verified; expected texts regenerated with tools/expected_from_measured.py.

contract.invariants[2], instructions[0], instructions[4] and instructions[7] now name build-evidence (design rule 3 and F-b1-04 for the pair, F-b3-18 for the interface surviving the swap, F-part-c-04 with agentic-stack for a criterion that can fail); the folded facet's instructions[8] pair was rewritten to one build-evidence pointer, folded composes_with.builds_on is ['build-evidence','cap-agent-runtime'], and references/usage.md names agentic-stack for the caller doctrine.

instructions[0] and instructions[6] now name build-evidence (the row already named cap-document-validation, which survives, so the half-updated sentence is whole again); the folded facet's instructions[8] pair was rewritten to one build-evidence pointer, folded composes_with.builds_on is ['build-evidence','cap-tool-access'], and references/usage.md names agentic-stack for the caller doctrine.

adapters[1].swap_procedure now says what code path differs rather than only who owns the list: with the second adapter the catalogue is read at bind time out of a response from a process this platform does not run and cannot restart, over a transport it does not terminate; every input schema the argument check runs against is authored there and may change between two binds; and an undeclared or withdrawn tool is refused inside that process, so the refusal arrives as a problem to be mapped rather than one raised here - the path a second endpoint of ours would never exercise.

fixed by the reference-link sweep (commits 440440e and 4128552, which also taught tools/validate_skills.py to refuse a reference link to a file that does not exist). Verified here: the three progressive-disclosure rows now name references/cap-telemetry-implement-telemetry-implementation.md, references/xc-correlation-correlation-audit.md and references/xc-correlation-implement-migration-and-wiring.md, every references/*.md path named anywhere in the skill resolves on disk, and validate_skills.py --only cap-telemetry reports 0 errors, 0 warnings.

contract.invariants[3] and [4] now name build-evidence, with invariants[4] saying which part it owns ('the general interface-versioning discipline'); adapters[0].swap_procedure points at references/cap-telemetry-implement.md rather than at a sibling skill that no longer exists; references/usage.md names agentic-stack for the caller doctrine. The folded objects' pointers to build-adapter-pair, build-definition-of-done and build-evidence-record were remapped in the same pass, and folded xc-correlation's used_by entry xc-enforcement-chain now reads xc-guarantees.

instructions[8] now sends a reader to both correlation references with one clause each: references/xc-correlation.md for the stamp, derive_child, audit and reassemble operations and the audit's zero-omission criterion over a run's whole population, and references/xc-correlation-implement.md for the migration off inherited trace context and the per-adapter conformance subsets.

Description now reads 'Traces, metrics and logs any collector ingests' and carries an audit clause: 'when auditing that every log record and problem object carries the run id'. To stay inside the 60-word cap (it is exactly 60) the wording was tightened ('run ids on explicit attributes set at dispatch, not trace parentage', 'where run ids live') and the weakest clause, 'when adopting an attribute naming convention', was dropped; the mapping-table subject is still reachable through 'what a unit of work emits' and 'when swapping an observability backend'.

declined.why: The split the fix asks for is already inside each row and flipping origin would cost accuracy elsewhere. Each of the four operation names carries its own disclosure in the name field ('call name is ours; sessions are one of the four things the standard itself standardizes', and the same for prompts, streaming and file permissions) and each output ends '(proposed)', so a reader is told exactly which half X-cap-agent-runtime-002 supports - the areas - and which half is ours. Marking all four origin=proposed would move cap-agent-runtime's proposed share from 17/58 (29.3%) to 21/58 (36.2%), over the 30 percent budget the row-71 sourcing pass was run to restore, and would add no information the rows do not already state. No record in kb/research.jsonl names ACP's actual method names, so there is nothing better to cite; the standards row keeps version_status unverified and cap-tool-access's first open question is the model for how that is carried.

Criterion unchanged; expected_design and expected_failure_design rewritten (R71B-001, R71B-003).

definitions_of_done_remeasured.note: Both skills went through one or two rejected measure runs first: tools/measure.py compares a whole-tree digest across the breakage, and concurrent edits by other row-71 agents (compose-workflow, harness/xc-compensation, kb/ceremonies/71-improve-b.json) tripped its restore check. Each was re-run until the restore verified; harness/ is clean and binding.json is at HEAD.

render_check: python3 tools/render_skill.py --check over all four exits 0: SKILL.md and every references/<former>.md are the current render of skill.json.
summary: 13 of 14 findings applied, 1 declined (R71B-008, the ACP operation origins). The block is closed: cap-isolation's folded implement facet now carries the same second adapter as the body, E-swap-candidate-gvisor per RP-005, and the definition of done says which binding stands for it. cap-isolation's expected_failure_design now describes the failure breakage A actually produces, and cap-agent-runtime's criterion ends in a per-adapter cancellation assertion, so its rendered Expected and Expected failure quote stop_reason and declared_gap_honoured instead of repeating cap-isolation's containment summary. Every pointer to a skill the fold removed (build-adapter-pair, build-definition-of-done, build-evidence-record, build-interface-versioning, cap-consumption, xc-enforcement-chain) is rewritten by name across the four bodies, their folded objects and their references/usage.md. Both re-measured definitions of done are measured with a real run; all four skills report 0 errors, 0 warnings and current renders.
